notes:
I don't have any notes on Ezekiel 13 for you yet. I tried to load the first six sources (Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub, Precept Austin and the NET Bible notes), but my code failed before I could read the results. When I tried to fix it, the tool told me I had used all my calls for this turn.

So I haven't actually read anything from those pages, and your rules say I can only report what I read, with a URL for each point. Writing verse notes now would mean guessing or relying on memory, so I've left them out.

**What I'll do next, if you ask me to continue:**
1. **Traditional reading:** read the six sources above, then add Pulpit Commentary, Matthew Henry, Barnes and others from StudyLight and Bible Hub, plus any Ezekiel 13 sermons on Ligonier, The Gospel Coalition, Desiring God and Spurgeon.org.
2. **Differences between Protestant traditions:** search each tradition's sites for verses 10–16 (the "peace when there is no peace" and whitewashed wall passage) and verses 17–23 (the women prophets and their charms). That means Wesley's notes for Methodists, Pneuma Review, Sam Storms and the Assemblies of God for Pentecostals and charismatics, and the LCMS and 1517 for Lutherans. I'll only report a difference if their own teachers actually state it.
3. **Other views:** check the NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship (for example, what the charms and veils in verse 18 were). Check New Advent, Catholic.com and OCA for Catholic and Orthodox readings. Search Got Questions and The Gospel Coalition for criticism of prosperity or word-of-faith "peace" preaching that uses this chapter.

Just reply "continue" and I'll start. Verses I can't find sources for will be left out, as you asked.
